hero.subtitle_html: Schwändi b. Schwanden GL, Post -> Vorder Glärnisch -- SAC T5+ | ~1608 m gain | ~11.9 km | ~5h

intro_html:
Vorder Glärnisch is for alpine hikers what Glärnisch is for climbers: an exciting tour to a fabulous viewpoint. The view down to Glarus from Vorder Glärnisch is even more impressive than from Vrenelisgärtli. The city of Glarus burnt down 150 years ago and was rebuilt as a planned city with a geometrical street layout, which, viewed from the summit, looks like a scale model. The ascent on the steep south face with its two huge gullies is more interesting than the usual white-blue marked route on the barren north face which has scree and rubble.

Vorder Glärnisch offers an impressive view deep down to Glarus. There is a summit cross and book. Besides the popular usual ascent from Hintersackberg, Vorder Glärnisch with its open faces on all sides offers an almost unlimited choice of routes, which are mostly on steep grassy slopes (up to 60°). Stöckli (P. 986), Forenstogg (P. 1484) and Gleiterhorn (P. 1623) are secondary summits or offshoots of the ridge, which can be climbed on various routes, but are not really targets in their own right. Schwösteren / Schwestern (P. 1947) is the last of the original three towers on the north-east ridge. Two of them collapsed in the last few centuries. There is the so called «Pandurenweg» which leads across Stöckli from Unter Sagg to Fadenwald.

getting_there.by_car_html: Drive to Schwändi near Schwanden in Canton Glarus via the A3 motorway (exit Niederurnen). Parking in Schwändi. For the traverse variant, arrange a second car at Klöntalersee or use public transport for the return.

day_plans.title: Day 1
rows: Depart Schwändi (701 m); ascend through forest
Above treeline (~1400 m); alpine terrain begins
Approach steep T5+ section; scrambling with exposure
Upper ridge — exposed terrain, require sure-footedness
Summit Vorder Glärnisch (2328 m); rest and panorama
Arrive Klöntalersee; bus or second car to return

lapse_rate.example_html: Example: Glarus forecast 15–25 °C → summit ≈ +3 °C to +13 °C. The Vorder Glärnisch is exposed to westerly winds.

weather.season_html: July–September is best. The T5+ terrain requires completely dry conditions. Snow lingers on north aspects into July. Thunderstorm risk high in summer afternoons — start early.

takeaways_html: The south-side ascent via Schwändisienen is steep and exposed, with passages up to T5+; very exposed or craggy sections are secured with chains.
Descent to Klöntalersee via Hintersackberg is steep but manageable thanks to a well-designed alpine hiking trail (T4).
Route-finding skills and sure-footedness are essential; conditions vary greatly and the grassy slopes can reach 60° steepness.

reports.title: Vorder Glärnisch (2328m) Südaufstieg via Schwändisienen
bullets_html: South-side ascent via Schwändisienen; steep grassy slopes and rocky bands.
Impressive panorama from the summit — Glarus city layout visible as a scale model below.

reports.title: Vorder Glärnisch (2328 m) - Überschreitung S-N
bullets_html: South-to-north traverse; direct ascent through couloir to Furggle with somewhat brittle rock.
Rockfall is a latent hazard in the couloir passage; stable holds found throughout.

reports.title: Vorder Glärnisch (2328 m) - hike from Hinter Sackberg
bullets_html: Ascent from Hinter Sackberg following white-blue-white trail markings.
Perfect weather conditions; summit reached in about 3 hours from trailhead.

safety_html: SAC grade T5+ — check conditions before departure.
Turn back if thunderstorms develop — lightning risk above treeline is extreme.
